pr_title: bluetooth: host: conn: Utilize conn_set_state in conn_destroy
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/54542 , which highlighted a bug in bt_disable, where if you have pending tx packets for a connection and then call bt_disable, it will assert. 

Previously we would call conn_cleanup for all connections,
however this had multiple problems such as:
-Not destroying conn->tx_pending packets and causing an assert
-Calling conn_cleanup for connectable adv, triggering
disconnected callback

Now we will use bt_conn_set_state to manage the teardown of
connections correctly. First, if in connected or disconnecting,
set state to disconnect complete. Then for all states, set
state to disconnected. This will carry out proper cleanup
and teardown when required.

To do this, it was required to keep the tx_thread open as
this is used in disconnecting teardown, so this has been
moved to below the conn_cleanup_all call.

Signed-off-by: Sean Madigan <sean.madigan@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments:
@sean-madigan Have this been verified to fix the issue? 

If so, please add `fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/54542` in the PR description

issue_context.title: Bluetooth pending tx packets assert on disable
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Fatal error (assert) on disabling Bluetooth when a pending transaction (notification).

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using? **nRF52840 DK**
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue? **not enable asserts or add delays before disabling Bluetooth** 
 - Is this a regression?  **no**

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.checkout on  https://github.com/ktaborowski/sdk-zephyr/tree/zephyrproject-bt-notify-and-disconnect
2. cd zephyr/samples/bluetooth/peripheral
3.  west build -p -b nrf52840dk_nrf52840
4. Connect nRF52840 DK board (PCA10056)
5. west flash
6. Subscribe to notification e.g. with nRF Connect App

![nrfconnect_1_connect](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52448413/217240688-9013dc30-cdd0-469b-987a-2aac87403d71.png)

7. Wait a few seconds, device disconnects automatically 

**Expected behavior**
Device disconnects, no fault.

**Impact**
We are facing the same issues in more complex application (prepared dumb sample for easy reproduction).

review_comments: we don't need to handle the `connecting` states?
As `bt_conn_set_state` has handling for the state change `BT_CONN_CONNECTING->BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED` I thought this was a safe operation.
Hmm, looking at `bt_conn_set_state`, is there actually any reason why we don't unconditionally call `bt_conn_set_state(BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE)`?

As there is specific handling for changing state `BT_CONN_CONNECTING/BT_CONN_CONNECTING_ADV` etc to `BT_CONN_DISONNECTED`, whereas `BT_CONN_CONNECTED/BT_CONN_DISCONNECTING` are designed to go through `BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE`
